about.profile.statement: I’m a third-year electrical engineering student at the American University of the Middle East, {1:on the Dean’s Honors List}. I design at every layer of a system — {2:a RISC-V core taken from RTL to GDSII}, {3:boards laid out for vision and navigation}, and {4:the test infrastructure that validates them}.
about.profile.note.2: CLEAVE — RV32I core, DRC/LVS-clean sky130 GDSII.
about.profile.note.3: NERONA (STM32N6 NPU) and AZIMUTH (ESP32-S3 sensor fusion).
about.profile.note.4: Lear — a 5.5-hour validation pass cut to about five minutes.

about.exp.note: Build and release engineering for automotive electronic-systems validation.
about.exp.a1: Designed and built CONDUIT, a local-first release-control dashboard that joins Azure DevOps with Palantir Foundry and auto-summarizes deployment logs. It replaced a multi-page manual review and was adopted by full-time engineers.
about.exp.a2: Debugged failing LIN-bus lighting and engine-cranking security-access test scripts across the release pipeline, clearing most logged errors and restoring clean sign-off builds.
about.exp.a3: Found and patched a CI gate defect that let pull requests with zero linked work items report as passing.
about.hil.title: One validation pass, re-architected.
about.hil.before: Test cases ran one after another, and a hang could stall a full pass for up to 5.5 hours.
about.hil.after: I rebuilt the runner to execute cases in parallel. A full pass now takes about five minutes.
about.hil.aria: Diagram: a validation pass moving from sequential test cases, with a hang of up to 5.5 hours, to parallel cases that finish in about five minutes.
